data.narrative: Produced a rigorous Failure Mode Analysis covering 6 external dependencies (including often-overlooked DNS and container runtime/clock skew) and 13 prioritized failure modes classified by probability, impact, and transient-vs-permanent nature. Empirically executed live failure simulations for database unavailability and 1ms outbound provider timeouts, then implemented structured 503/504 failure-mode error classification in globalErrorHandler and verified every path.

dimension_scores.observation: Accounted for container-level failure modes including cgroup OOM kills, ephemeral storage exhaustion, and decoupled /live vs /ready probes to prevent crash-loop thrashing during network partitions.
dimension_scores.evidence: Documented container memory caps (512Mi), stateless stdout logging, and decoupled liveness/readiness behavior in docs/failure-mode-analysis.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Built repeatable failure-simulation and re-verification scripts validating error status codes, Retry-After headers, metrics counters, and structured failure_mode telemetry.
dimension_scores.evidence: Created scripts/verify-module-05-failure-modes.ts and scripts/verify-module-05-fix.ts passing 100% of assertions.

dimension_scores.observation: Instrumented explicit failure_mode and transient boolean fields on infrastructure error logs so on-call responders can immediately distinguish DNS, timeout, and read-only storage faults from application bugs.
dimension_scores.evidence: Verified structured JSON error output with failure_mode='dns_resolution_failure', 'dependency_timeout', and 'database_unavailable_or_readonly'.

dimension_scores.observation: Demonstrated senior-level failure analysis: recognized why slow grey failures are more dangerous than hard outages, distinguished transient vs permanent faults to prevent harmful retries, and surfaced non-obvious DNS, clock-skew, and read-only replica failover scenarios.
dimension_scores.evidence: Authored 13-entry failure mode matrix, cascading failure propagation map, and probability-x-impact top-3 risk ranking in docs/failure-mode-analysis.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Adopted Fail-Closed as the security-first default while explicitly designing Fail-Open degradation for Redis caching, async analytics queues, and secondary notification channels.
dimension_scores.evidence: Mapped per-dependency fail-closed vs fail-open stances and implemented HTTP 503 + Retry-After: 5 / HTTP 504 responses in apps/api/src/middleware/error.middleware.ts.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered a crisp, scannable operational Failure Mode Analysis document pairing dependency timeout inventories, ASCII cascading failure diagrams, empirical simulation tables, and remediation priorities.
dimension_scores.evidence: Authored docs/failure-mode-analysis.md with complete tables and empirical simulation gap comparisons.

strengths: Empirical chaos discipline: simulated both DB downtime and 1ms external timeouts to capture real latency/status gaps instead of guessing
Nuanced failure taxonomy: cleanly separates transient vs permanent faults and explains why retrying 401/403 or read-only errors amplifies outages
Systems-level blind-spot detection: proactively included DNS failures, NTP clock skew, and read-only replica partial failures
data.recommendation: Use the Risk #1 priority from your Failure Mode Analysis (slow/failing external notification providers) to drive circuit breaker, timeout, and jittered retry implementation in Module 06.

public_evidence.student_action: Authored comprehensive Failure Mode Analysis covering 6 external dependencies, 13 failure modes, transient-vs-permanent classification, and live simulation gap findings.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Dependency timeout inventory, cascading failure ASCII diagram, probability-x-impact top-3 ranking, and simulated DB outage & 1ms timeout tables
public_evidence.proof: Backed by live execution metrics from scripts/verify-module-05-failure-modes.ts (503 in 8.39ms, TimeoutError in 3ms).
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates ability to anticipate grey failures, partial read-only failovers, and cascading exhaustion before writing resilience code.

public_evidence.student_action: Added structured infrastructure failure classification returning HTTP 503/504 with Retry-After headers and explicit failure_mode telemetry.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Classifies TimeoutError/AbortError (504), ENOTFOUND/EAI_AGAIN (503), and read-only/ECONNREFUSED storage errors (503) without leaking stack traces
public_evidence.proof: Automated verification via scripts/verify-module-05-fix.ts confirmed all 3 status codes, headers, and structured log fields.
public_evidence.ability: Failure-Aware HTTP Semantics & Structured Fault Classification
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Improves client retry behavior and dramatically reduces MTTR by distinguishing infrastructure faults from programmer exceptions.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Enumerated 13 dependency failure modes with probability, user impact, current vs desired handling, and risk ranking.
Explained and simulated how slow dependencies hold sockets and exhaust pools far more dangerously than instant ECONNREFUSED.
Separated retryable transient faults from non-retryable permanent errors (invalid credentials, malformed payloads).
Enforced fail-closed for auth/primary writes while opting cache and async queues into fail-open degradation.

teaching_approaches.concept: Empirical Failure Simulation & Partial Failure Handling
teaching_approaches.detail: Simulated DB outage, 1ms outbound timeouts, DNS ENOTFOUND, and read-only replica errors to close theoretical-vs-actual gaps.
